releases.headline: Subshell 0.87: one size for the whole app, save for offline, and a calmer first start
highlights: Settings › Appearance › Size › UI size makes the whole app smaller or larger, from 85 to 110 %: bars, buttons, lists, dialogs and text.
Save for offline in the Home menu keeps the top 50 posts, their comments and pictures on your phone for when you have no signal.
A new setting, Show NSFW media, shows NSFW pictures and videos without a tap on each one. Spoilers stay covered.
New installs set up hand, look, content and notifications in one short flow, and Backup & restore now says what a backup holds.
Fixes: a crash when a link or notification opened the app, "r/name" searches in Discover, a play button flash before autoplay, comment jumps that stopped short, and more.

releases.headline: Subshell 0.86: reply from notifications, RedGIFs with sound and a faster inbox
highlights: Private messages and chats arrive as conversation notifications, and you can reply right from the notification.
RedGIFs clips play with sound, videos pause the moment you switch tabs, and headset or Bluetooth buttons play and pause them.
The inbox refreshes several times faster, and messages you read elsewhere no longer count as unread.
You can post to your own profile, and galleries posted from the app show their images again.
Subshell opens straight to your feeds, and switching dark mode or text size keeps your place, drafts and votes.

releases.headline: Subshell 0.85: a security update for sign-in, notifications and media
highlights: Signing out of an account now also removes Reddit's web login, unless another signed-in account still uses it.
The sign-in window opens only Reddit, Google and Apple pages, and a sign-in that fails is also withdrawn at Reddit.
Other apps can no longer open accounts or screens in subshell. Notifications from before the update just open the app.
With the app lock on, the recent-apps preview stays blank on Android 12 and older, and new-post notifications from hidden communities don't name them.
Post images and videos load only from public addresses, images and GIFs share one memory limit, and nothing is written to the system log.

releases.headline: Subshell 0.84: new-post notifications, text selection and one sign-in for everything
highlights: Get a notification when a community you choose has a new post: "Notify about new posts" in the community's ⋮ menu (up to 10 communities).
Long press to select and copy text in posts, comments and messages, with Android's Copy, Share and Translate.
Sign-in asks for every permission once. Modmail, mod log and the wiki no longer ask again (accounts signed in before approve one more time).
If sign-in stops working because Reddit or RedReader changed something, you can edit the redirect URI and user agent yourself, in Settings or during setup.
Short confirmations such as "Muted r/x" now disappear by themselves.

releases.headline: Subshell 0.83: choose how posts look, pinned posts first, and pinch to zoom videos
highlights: Choose how posts look: Large, Compact, List or Grid, from the view button beside the feed (and in Settings).
A community's pinned posts now come first in every sort, as cards or as compact highlights.
Pinch to zoom videos in the full-screen player (turn it on in Settings).
A fresh look: Google's Material Symbols icons, Material 3 Expressive motion, and dynamic colour on by default.
More reliable: one unreadable post no longer breaks a whole feed, removed images say so instead of retrying, and the inbox sync retries on a shaky network.

releases.headline: Subshell 0.82: a new comment composer, a smaller app and open source
highlights: Replying is rebuilt: a quick reply card sits on the keyboard, and Expand opens a full-screen editor with formatting and a preview of your comment.
subshell is about two-thirds smaller (7.5 MB instead of 24.6 MB) and starts more evenly, thanks to code shrinking and a startup profile.
If subshell closes unexpectedly, the next start offers to send a diagnostic report. Nothing leaves your phone unless you choose to send it.
subshell's source code is now public under GPL-3.0, one snapshot per release, at github.com/brealorg/subshell-source-public.
Updated to the newest Material 3 components.

releases.headline: Subshell 0.81: feed videos keep their shape
highlights: Fixed: tall and very wide videos in the feed were stretched and cut off at the edge while playing.
Mention people in comments: type @ or u/ for people from the thread, then Reddit's people search.
Subshell checks for updates when you come back to it, so a new release shows up within the hour.
The update dialog can turn on update notifications if Android has them switched off.

releases.headline: Subshell 0.80: Material 3 throughout, a new video player and better accessibility
highlights: Material 3 throughout: one top bar per screen, a navigation rail on tablets and foldables, list rows and segmented choices in Settings.
Video: a new seek bar with live frames, playback options in post and full screen, speed, double-tap skip, hold for 2x and picture-in-picture (each optional).
Wi-Fi only autoplay now really holds autoplay on mobile data; playing video keeps the screen on, and unplugging headphones pauses.
A Video group in Settings: subtitles, audio language, timeline size, quality and where the playback options show.
Better contrast, screen-reader labels and large-text layouts across the app.
Defaults reviewed: the theme follows the system, unread markers are on, and a one-time tip points to Settings.
Comments removed by a moderator are marked Removed in the thread.
NSFW: searches follow Show NSFW posts, quarantined communities can be opted into, banned and private ones say why; optional random NSFW community.
Errors appear in one tray instead of pop-ups; an image that can never load offers Open in browser.
Images linked over http load over https; a link to an image host stays a link.
Fixes: GIFs on your own profile autoplay again, lists without a top bar scroll by touch, Hidden tab for local accounts, link decoding on Android 8-12.
Many internal checks replaced by behaviour tests, and every land now runs a lint gate.

releases.headline: Subshell 0.79: saved searches, RedGIFs in the app, Reddit favorites sync and a full review of the code.
highlights: New: saved searches in the Search hub, an optional scroll position indicator, RedGIFs clips in the app (with Show NSFW posts) and favorites synced with Reddit.
Reddit emotes, GIFs and images show inline in posts and comments and can be edited; spoilers stay hidden until tapped; escapes, nested styles and lists render right.
Safer writing: a post, comment, message or moderator action whose answer was lost is checked with Reddit instead of sent twice, and drafts survive restarts.
Accounts stay apart: votes, scroll positions, lists and notifications no longer cross between accounts; a notification for another account switches to it.
Fewer crashes and stalls: the app returns where you were after Android closes it, large photos no longer crash previews, and slow work left the main thread.
Accessibility: switches, choices and buttons announce what they are and their state, touch targets are larger, and auto-hiding controls follow the system timeout.
Correctness: votes, refreshes, paging, search results, markdown, flair and moderator tools now do what they show, and Retry picks up where a load failed.
No lost work: drafts, replies and moderator actions survive Android closing the app or a missing answer from Reddit, and backups read back everything they hold.
Privacy and security: names and ids stay out of release logs, turning a protection off needs the device unlock, and comment images load only from known image hosts.
Speed: lists, settings, backups and links read their data off the main thread, caches are capped, and long threads load more replies on their own.
Also: inbox notifications are on by default, shares and links open in the Subshell you already have, numbers follow your language and word filters match whole words.
Removed: video downloads. Videos stream; anything an older version downloaded can be deleted in Settings.

releases.headline: Subshell 0.78: app lock, private user notes, sharing into Subshell and content filters everywhere.
highlights: Optional app lock: unlock with biometrics or the screen lock, choose when it locks again, and optionally hide what notifications say.
Private notes and coloured tags on Reddit users, shown next to their name, with an opt-in to include them in backups.
Share links, text and images from other apps into Subshell to start a post (optional, off by default).
Content filters now work on community pages, custom feeds and search, can be limited to one community, and can show how many posts they hide.
Many more Reddit links open inside the app: share links, images and videos, profile tabs, searches, custom feeds and wiki pages.
Also new: find in thread, jump between top-level comments, in-app text size, pure black theme, launcher shortcuts, gallery downloads, Giphy GIFs and post flair emoji.

releases.headline: Seventh public beta of Subshell.
highlights: Comment author avatars in threads, with a setting to turn them off.
An open drawer closes on Back or a scrim tap even with comment swipe actions on.
Moderators can send a removal message after removing a post or comment, with saved responses that can be backed up.
One composer family everywhere: the same editor, formatting bar, preview and buttons in posts, comments, chat, modmail and New message.
Editing a post or comment asks before discarding unsaved changes.

releases.headline: Sixth public beta of Subshell.
highlights: Returning to Home or a community from a post keeps your place in the feed; cached feeds revalidate on first entry and again after fifteen minutes.
Internal restructuring of app state into focused components and removal of unused screens, with no intended visible changes.
Same changes as beta.5, republished so the in-app update check can offer it.

releases.headline: Fifth public beta of Subshell.
highlights: Returning to Home or a community from a post keeps your place in the feed; cached feeds revalidate on first entry and again after fifteen minutes.
Internal restructuring of app state into focused components and removal of unused screens, with no intended visible changes.

releases.headline: Fourth public beta of Subshell.
highlights: Native Reddit crossposting now supports destination selection, flair, review, publishing, and immediate canonical post presentation.
Posts can now be followed and unfollowed directly from the post overflow menu.
Community user flair support now includes selecting your own flair and richer author flair presentation.
Configurable swipe actions are available for posts and comments, with gesture arbitration and haptic feedback.
Cached Home and community feeds now refresh automatically on re-entry, and inline comment images open in the shared fullscreen viewer.
Video looping is available as an optional setting, alongside refinements to Accounts and searchable Settings.

releases.headline: Third public beta of Subshell.
highlights: Expanded Mod Tools with reports, content controls, Mod Log, user management, and moderator team administration.
Portable backup and restore now covers more community state and optional post drafts with transactional restore.
Improved Reddit video reliability with poster continuity, returned-feed audio fixes, fallback handling, and landscape controls.
More flexible comment hierarchy and collapse presentation.
Built-in GitHub beta update awareness with What's New and an in-app changelog.

releases.headline: Second public beta of Subshell.
highlights: Adaptive Subscriptions/community workspace improvements.
Better Modmail selection continuity in adaptive layouts.
Stronger concealment of sensitive preloaded video before reveal.
Clearer Reddit Client ID onboarding and setup guidance.
Additional diagnostics support for beta troubleshooting.

releases.headline: First public beta of Subshell.
highlights: First signed public beta distributed through GitHub Releases.
